subject: ClearCart checkout delays — request-latency outliers and immediate actions
messages:
From: Tim Carter <tim@clearcart.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearCart Engineering <eng@clearcart.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T02:18:00-07:00
Subject: ClearCart: sudden API latency spikes impacting checkout (URGENT)

Hi Hannah —

We started seeing a large increase in checkout latencies on Redwood’s hosted endpoint around 01:40 UTC this morning. Impact: ~8% of checkout requests are hitting >2.5s (p99 ~3.2s) and a small but material uptick in 5xx errors tied to timeouts. This is affecting live traffic across US region; we had to temporarily throttle a demo rollout.

Attached is a short sample of request IDs and timings (latency-sample-logs.csv). Key example request IDs: rc-7f9a2, rc-7f9a8, rc-7f9bc. We see the backend returning 200s but the end-to-end time is high; some traces show long wait times before the first byte.

Can you confirm whether this is a configuration issue on our end or something on the Redwood side? We’re under a tight promo window and need an ETA — please escalate.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Carter
VP Engineering, ClearCart
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Carter <tim@clearcart.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-15T02:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearCart: sudden API latency spikes impacting checkout (URGENT)

Tim — thanks for the heads up and the sample. I’ve opened an internal incident and looped SRE (laura), support (priyom), and CS escalation (rishi). We’ll triage immediately and come back with a plan in the next 30–45 mins.

Initial asks for us while we dig in: can your team share the exact endpoint path and the typical request payload size (or a sanitized example)? That helps rule out request-shape regressions.

Proposed immediate coordination:
- SRE will check for router queueing/backpressure and concurrency caps.
- If we see dedicated-pool saturation we can temporarily bump capacity and/or route to a compatible fallback variant.
- We’ll also review recent rollout traffic and any config changes.

I’ve scheduled a 30m bridge (calendar invite to follow) at 02:55 UTC. If you prefer a direct call sooner, let me know. We’ll keep you updated on actions and a timeline.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-15T03:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ClearCart: sudden API latency spikes impacting checkout (TECH TRIAGE)

Summary of what I’m seeing from the first-cut telemetry:
- Ingress router shows sustained queue depth increases starting 01:38 UTC for the ClearCart tenant pool.
- Concurrency cap on their dedicated pool (configured at 320 concurrent tokens) is being hit repeatedly; backend workers are queuing requests rather than shedding.
- KV cache warmup is not the main issue (hit rates normal). The long wait occurs pre-worker (request sits in router queue).
- A small set of requests (~2% of keys) show long kernel spin waiting during tokenization/hot-path but not enough to explain the magnitude alone.

Immediate mitigations tried:
1) Auto-scale hint sent to orchestration layer to add 2x workers to ClearCart dedicated pool (in flight) — this should reduce queueing within 2–4 minutes once nodes are healthy.
2) We can enable a fallback route to a smaller, lower-latency model variant (compatible with their contract) to reduce tail latency for non-critical requests.
3) If queueing persists, enable a temporary aggressive request-shedding policy for bulk/batch endpoints to favor interactive checkout traffic.

Attachments: router-trace-20270615.json, p99-sample.png (short traces and percentile chart).

I’ll keep monitoring and will post an update when scale is effective or if we see errors rise.

— Laura
Senior SRE, Redwood Runtime
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-15T03:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: ClearCart: escalation and customer-facing plan

Quick escalation note for execs / AM:
- Impact: intermittent p99 degradation for ClearCart checkouts causing aborted flows for ~5% of sessions during the 01:38–02:20 UTC window.
- Root cause (current hypothesis): request router queueing due to transient surge that hit their configured concurrency cap; orchestration did not scale fast enough because the surge pattern looked like short spikes.

Action items completed/in-flight:
- +2 worker scale request accepted by orchestration; expected warm start + readiness in ~3–5 minutes (APPLIED).
- Fallback routing to smaller model variant enabled for non-payment paths (APPLIED).
- Temporary targeted rate-limit for bulk endpoints to protect checkout surface (PENDING toggle by 03:20 UTC).
- Created Jira: SRE-1293 to track follow-up (investigate autoscaler heuristics and fast-start warm pools).

Customer compensation recommendation: offer a one-month service credit and a joint post-mortem within 48 hours. I’ll draft the acceptance language for legal if you want.

I’ll join the bridge and can present a short timeline for resolution to the ClearCart team.

— Rishi
Director, Customer Operations
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Carter <tim@clearcart.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-15T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearCart: sudden API latency spikes impacting checkout (RESOLVED - follow up)

Tim — quick executive summary and sorry again for the disruption earlier today.

What happened (tl;dr): a short traffic surge hit ClearCart’s dedicated tenant pool and the router queues grew while the autoscaler took a few minutes to add healthy workers, producing a long-tail latency increase and a small rise in timeouts.

What we did:
- Scaled the dedicated worker pool (+2 nodes) and applied a fallback route to a compatible, lower-latency model variant for non-payment requests.
- Enabled a temporary selective rate-limit for bulk endpoints to prioritize checkout traffic.
- Opened Jira SRE-1293 to tune the autoscaler for fast spikes and pre-warmed worker heuristics.

Customer timeline: full mitigation completed by ~03:25 UTC; p99 returned to expected range within two warm-up minutes. We’re continuing monitoring and will include a detailed post-mortem.

Offer: we’d like to provide a one-month usage credit for the window impacted and schedule a 45-minute post-mortem with your engineering team within 48 hours.

Next steps:
- I’ll send the credit terms and post-mortem invite.
- Our SRE team (Laura) will share a short technical write-up (router traces + recommendation).

Apologies for the outage — your team’s patience helped us remediate quickly. Please let me know if you want an accelerated remediation credit or a different remedy.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0139

Attachments: latency-sample-logs.csv, router-trace-20270615.json, p99-sample.png
